messages:
incident-bot: SLO burn-rate alert firing: service=redwood-inference-hosted, burn=120% over 10m, current-window=10m, multi-window=5m/10m/1h. pager: yes. https://monitoring.company/internal/alerts/2345

maria: seeing the pages. investigating now. looks like a traffic spike from a single customer causing request latency -> client timeouts. paging to oncall per policy.

sam: @maria thanks. is this impacting end-user queries or just internal retries?

maria: user-facing errors up ~3.4% for the last 12m. some 5xx and some higher latency tail. customers in us-west mostly.

lee: I'm watching the runtime queues. CPU on pool-gpu-3 spiked when KV cache warmed, batching got longer. might be a batching pattern issue with sequence lengths.

maria: rolling a temporary patch to cap batch size to reduce tail. deploying now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maria at commit abc123 -> deploy/redwood/runtime#cap-batch. CI OK.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded in us-west (canary) at +2m.

maria: canary looks good, tail latency down 40% on canary hosts. promoting to remainder.

incident-bot: SLO burn-rate alert resolved for 10m window, still firing on 5m window (burn=110%).

sam: since the 5m window is noisy during short spikes, can we revisit paging policy? it's paging on any single-window >100% which creates rapid pages for transient blips.

lee: agreed. suggest requiring either multi-window confirmation or a sustained 5m->15m escalation. e.g., page only if: (burn_5m > 100% AND burn_15m > 80%) OR burn_1h > 125%.

ingrid: I'll put together a dashboard for burn across windows and customer attribution so we can see if spikes are single-customer. want it in the SLO health dash.

maria: oncall handoff in 10m, @sam will take the next shift. leaving notes: mitigated via cap-batch, rollback plan ready, customer impact ~3.4% errors, affected region us-west.

oncall-rotation: Paging handoff: maria -> sam. please ack when accepted.

sam: ack. taking over. quick summary: cap-batch deployed, monitoring more stable but 5m window still flapping. propose we adjust alert rule to reduce noise and create a follow-up change to SLO policy.

lee: here's a candidate alert rule snippet for the monitoring team (feel free to copy):

```yaml
alert: SLOBurn-ManagedPaging
expr: (burn_5m > 1.0 && burn_15m > 0.8) || (burn_1h > 1.25)
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "SLO burn high for {{ $labels.service }}"
  runbook: "https://wiki.company/slo-burn-runbook"
```

sam: that looks reasonable. key change is adding `for: 2m` and multi-window gating. reduces pages for transient single-sample noise.

maria: also adding a label `root_cause_candidate` that we can set if a single-customer spike is identified, so ops can mute paging for known noisy customers pending contact.

ingrid: dash created: https://monitoring.company/dashboards/slo-burn-multiwindow. includes per-customer breakdown, windowed burn lines, and top-request patterns.

incident-bot: Note: a follow-up ticket was created -> CONF-589: "Refine SLO paging criteria and create multi-window dashboard" assigned to eng-sre.

sam: creating a short RFC for SLO paging policy changes: include multi-window gating, minimal `for` duration, and a temporary mute workflow for known-customer spikes. will post in #product once drafted.

maria: small post-incident actions
- update alert rule (lee's yaml) in monitoring repo
- add runbook step for muting customer alerts with audit trail
- add short-term tweak to paging criteria in oncall playbook
- follow up RFC for policy changes

sam: I've applied the new alert quieting rule in staging and will roll to prod in 15m unless objections.

lee: thumbs up. suggest adding a synthetic check: if per-customer QPS > X and bucketed sequences < Y then increase `for` to avoid premature pages.

ingrid: will add the customer heatmap tile to the dash.

sam: prod change applied. monitor for 1h. will report back.

incident-bot: SLO burn alert suppressed by new multi-window rule at 1956790200 for service=redwood-inference-hosted.

maria: thanks team. pages dropped to zero after the rule change. leaving a short incident note in the postmortem doc.

sam: filing follow-ups: CONF-590 (policy RFC), CONF-591 (monitoring rule PR), CONF-592 (runbook mute step). assigning owners.

lee: nice quick mitigation and good follow-up. recommend we measure false-positive page reduction over next 7 days.

ingrid: agreed — will include a weekly widget on the dash.

maria: handing off final logs and timeline to sam in the postmortem doc. handoff complete.

sam: ack received. I'll finish the postmortem and coordinate RFC. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
